verses.text: This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was surrounding Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was locked up in the courtyard of the guard at the palace of the king of Judah.

Zedekiah king of Judah had locked him up there. He said, "Why do you prophesy like this? You say, 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am going to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the Babylonians. He will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will speak to him face to face and see him with his own eyes.
He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and Zedekiah will stay there until I deal with him, says the LORD. If you fight against the Babylonians, you will not win.'"
Jeremiah said, "The LORD's message came to me:
'Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, is going to come to you and say, "Buy my field in Anathoth, because as my nearest relative you have the right to buy it."'

Then, just as the LORD had said, my cousin Hanamel came to me in the courtyard of the guard and said, 'Please buy my field in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin. You have the right to own it and to buy it back for the family. Buy it for yourself.' Then I knew this was the LORD's message.
So I bought the field in Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel and weighed out seventeen pieces of silver for him.
I signed the deed and sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed out the silver on the scales.
Then I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy containing the terms and conditions and the open copy.
I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah. I did this in front of my cousin Hanamel, the witnesses who had signed the deed, and all the Jews sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
In front of them all I gave Baruch these instructions:
'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Take these deeds, both the sealed copy and the open copy, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time.
For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Houses, fields, and vineyards will once again be bought in this land.'
After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
"Oh, Lord GOD! You made the heavens and the earth by your great power and your outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.
You show faithful love to thousands, but you also bring the consequences of the parents' sins on their children after them. You are the great and mighty God. The LORD of Armies is your name.
Your plans are great, and your deeds are mighty. Your eyes see everything people do, and you reward each person for how they live and for what they do.
You did miraculous signs and wonders in Egypt, and you still do them today, both in Israel and among all people. You have made a name for yourself that lasts to this day.
You brought your people Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
You gave them this land that you promised their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.
They came in and took it over, but they did not obey you or follow your law. They did nothing you commanded them to do. So you brought all this disaster on them.

Look, siege ramps have been built against the city to capture it. Because of war, famine, and disease, the city will be handed over to the Babylonians who are attacking it. What you said has happened, as you can see.
And yet, Lord GOD, you have told me, 'Buy the field with silver and call witnesses,' even though the city will be handed over to the Babylonians."
Then the LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Look, I am the LORD, the God of all people. Is anything too hard for me?
So this is what the LORD says: I am going to hand this city over to the Babylonians and to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

The Babylonians attacking this city will come in and set it on fire. They will burn it down, along with the houses where people made me angry by burning incense to Baal on the roofs and pouring out drink offerings to other gods.

The people of Israel and Judah have done nothing but evil in my sight since they were young. The people of Israel have done nothing but make me angry with the idols they made with their hands, says the LORD.
From the day this city was built until now, it has stirred up my anger and fury, so I must remove it from my sight.

This is because of all the evil the people of Israel and Judah have done to make me angry: they, their kings, their officials, their priests, their prophets, the people of Judah, and those living in Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to me, not their faces. I taught them again and again, but they would not listen or accept correction.
They set up their disgusting idols in the temple that is called by my name, and made it unclean.

They built high places for Baal in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, to sacrifice their sons and daughters in the fire to Molech. I never commanded them to do this. It never even entered my mind that they would do something so disgusting and make Judah sin."
"Now this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about this city. You are saying, 'It will be handed over to the king of Babylon through war, famine, and disease.'
But look, I will gather them from all the countries where I drove them in my anger, fury, and great rage. I will bring them back to this place and let them live in safety.
They will be my people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way of life, so that they will always respect me, for their own good and for the good of their children after them.
I will make a covenant with them that will last forever. I will never stop doing good to them. I will put respect for me in their hearts, so that they will never turn away from me.
I will enjoy doing good to them. I will faithfully plant them in this land with all my heart and all my soul."
This is what the LORD says: "Just as I have brought all this great disaster on these people, so I will bring them all the good things I have promised them.
Fields will be bought again in this land. You now say, 'It is a wasteland with no people or animals. It has been handed over to the Babylonians.'

But people will buy fields with silver, sign deeds, seal them, and call witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, in the villages around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah, in the towns of the hill country, the western foothills, and the Negev, because I will bring them back from captivity," says the LORD.
